original_question: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). A subgroup H of a right-orderable group G is said to be right-relatively convex if it is convex under some right ordering on G. Is the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group always a sublattice of the lattice of its subgroups?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.147 in the "New Problems" section of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim: it uses the same class of groups (right-orderable groups), the same notion of a subgroup being right-relatively convex (convex under some right ordering on G), and the same open question asking whether these subgroups form a sublattice inside the full subgroup lattice.
missing_details: Make the quantifier explicit: the question is whether the statement holds for every right-orderable group G.
For stand-alone clarity, spell out that a right-orderable group is one admitting a total order invariant under right multiplication.
Specify that the lattice is ordered by inclusion.
Unpack "sublattice of the lattice of subgroups" as closure under the subgroup-lattice meet and join, namely intersection and the subgroup generated by the union.
refined_question: For every group G that admits a right ordering (that is, a total order invariant under right multiplication), let RRC(G) be the set of subgroups H <= G that are convex with respect to some right ordering of G. Is RRC(G), ordered by inclusion, always a sublattice of the subgroup lattice Sub(G); equivalently in lattice-theoretic terms, whenever H,K are in RRC(G), must both H ∩ K and the subgroup generated by H ∪ K again belong to RRC(G)?
justification: The draft is already extremely close to the exact problem stated in the paper. The nearest official formulation is the problem entry itself, namely Problem 21.147. The adjacent Problem 21.148 asks a different question, about when the lattice is distributive and whether that is equivalent to being a chain, so it should not be merged into the rewrite. Because this source is a problem collection rather than a standard article developing notation through propositions and theorems, the only needed sharpening is to make the universal quantifier and the lattice operations explicit while keeping the scope identical to the original entry.
